newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand short maturities close with firm tone.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand short maturities close with firm tone.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

MCI -85 VS -87
* NZ bond curve ends steeper with short bonds in demand
* Market buffeted by dollar-yen move, MCI still focus
* No word from RBNZ taken as tacit acceptance of easing
The New Zealand bond yield curve ended steeper on Thursday with short bonds in demand.
Long bonds closed a point higher in yield at 7.60 percent but outperformed U.S. treasuries which had weakened on U.S. trade data.
The bank bill market maintained Wednesday afternoon's firm tone, growing more confident daily at the Reserve Bank's silence.
"The market is getting more confident each day that the Reserve Bank is comfortable with conditions," said one dealer.
Traders remain riveted to the Monetary Conditions Index, which held around minus 85 basis points, a level at which the RB last week expressed its discomfort.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed little changed but continues to be buffeted by volatile action in the dollar-yen and further choppy behaviour from that direction is predicted.
One dealer said there was general reluctance to buy the kiwi as more data confirmed weakness in the economy. That nervousness was undermining the TWI and encouraging the easing bias.
Thursday's wages data was almost exactly in line with expectations -- up 0.7 percent for the March quarter -- and did nothing to change perceptions the economy had slowed sharply.
"The data supports an easing bias," said one dealer.
Bond dealers said strength in the short bonds -- where the 2/00s finished three basis points down at 7.40 percent -- had fuelled talk of more euro issues.
"It feels like the curve wants to go steeper from here. It's flattened a lot in the last couple of weeks. But it's going to be pretty flows-driven," said an Auckland bond trader.
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
